Subject: Azura AI — post-call: topology, SLOs & next steps

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

What we heard (primary pain points)
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak inference windows (batching spikes causing p99 > 2s).
- High per-token cost from repeated context rebuilds and lack of KV cache reuse across requests.
- Regulatory requirement: data residency + encryption; procurement will likely ask for on-prem/VPC options and SOC2 evidence.

Stated goals (priority order)
1) p95 latency <= 150ms for generation up to 512 tokens under expected concurrency (target baseline: 200 concurrent sessions).
2) Sustained throughput of ~200–300 requests/sec for short-text workloads (avg payload 128 tokens).
3) Reduce inference unit cost ~30% vs current baseline through caching & quantization guidance.

High-level topology options we discussed
- Private (VPC) deployment with Dedicated GPU pools in us-west-2 (preferred for data residency).
- Hybrid: control plane in hosted Redwood, inference plane in dedicated customer VPC.
- Hosted fallback variant (quantized, slightly smaller model) for burst overflow.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Rishi to provide a short technical appendix with p50/p95/p99 projections across candidate models and suggested batch sizing (attached). (Rishi, EOD 2026-12-20)
- Jordan to share a draft topology diagram and SLO estimate spreadsheet for your procurement team. (Jordan, attached)
- Azura to send the security questionnaire and any specific compliance docs you need completed. (Ava / Procurement)
- Schedule a follow-up 30–45 minute deep-dive to walk the appendix and confirm model choice and node sizing. (All — propose Wed 12/22 or Thu 12/23)

Attachments included in this email: redwood-azura-topology-draft.pdf (draft topology/notes), slo-estimates-azura.csv (SLO estimate lookup). Please confirm receipt.

Thanks — looking forward to locking the plan so your engineers can validate performance on a short pilot.

Subject: Azura — technical appendix: latency & throughput projections (short summary)

Hi Ava / Jordan,

Following up with the technical appendix requested. Below is an executive-summary of the numbers plus recommended deployment patterns. The attached CSV has per-model, per-seqlen rows supporting these estimates. These are projections based on internal benchmarks on H100(80GB) and A100(80GB) nodes with Redwood's continuous-batching runtime and KV cache enabled. Real results will vary by prompt mix and tokenization.

Key assumptions
- Typical request: 128 tokens output, 64 tokens prompt.
- Warm cache (KV cache hit): repeated conversation continuation within same session ~60–80% hit expected with session-affinity.
- Batching behavior: continuous batching with max_batch configurable between 8–128; we model three regimes: small (8–16), medium (32–48), large (64–128).

Summary p50/p95/p99 (examples, single GPU H100 80GB, 70B model - 4-bit quantized path)
- Short requests (<=128 tokens output): p50 ~ 35–45ms, p95 ~ 110–140ms, p99 ~ 320–450ms (depends on batching and cold-starts).
- Medium requests (~512 tokens): p50 ~ 120–160ms, p95 ~ 420–650ms, p99 ~ 900–1400ms.

Throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec estimates)
- Single H100 80GB for 70B quantized (continuous batching, medium batch 32): ~1,250–1,600 tokens/sec => ~250–350 rps for short requests.
- A100 80GB is ~70–80% of H100 throughput in our tests for these models under identical configs.

Burst handling and tail latency mitigation
- Autoscaling with warm standby: maintain a pool sized for sustained load and add ephemeral nodes for bursts. Warm standby cut cold-start impact by ~60% in our bench.
- KV cache: for customer chat workloads, prefix/KV cache reuse reduces token compute ~25–40% depending on prompt overlap, directly dropping p95 and average cost.
- Admission control: use a priority queue for user-facing low-latency requests; non-urgent batchable requests routed to lower-priority pools (cost saving).

Model-family comparison (70B Llama vs 70B Mistral-ish) in 4-bit quantized path
- Mistral variants are often faster per-token (microarchitectural differences); on H100 we saw 10–18% higher throughput for equivalent quality in our internal evals. Memory footprint comparable.
- Latency p99 typically better for Mistral under identical batching due to fewer kernel invocations (observed in our kernel-selection paths).

Recommended deployment for Azura pilot
- Mode: Private VPC with Dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 (to meet residency).
- Node type: prefer H100 80GB for primary pool. A100 for overflow/burst is viable but expect ~20–30% lower throughput.
- Pool sizing: start with 4 H100 nodes (handles ~1k–1.4k rps short-requests with continuous batching, assuming ~70% cache hit), add autoscale policy to double for 30-minute bursts to handle 600 concurrent sessions without p95 degradation.
- Canary & rollouts: 5% canary traffic for model changes, automatic rollback on p95/p99 regressions or increase in error rate >1%.

Operational considerations
- Warm-up: pre-warm KV cache by replaying recent prefixes during deployments.
- Monitoring: token-level SLO dashboards (p50/p95/p99 by route), request-size heatmaps, and cost per request.
- Fallbacks: route to smaller quantized variant when queueing latency >100ms for user-facing routes.

Attachments: redwood-azura-technical-appendix.pdf (detailed tables & charts), slo-estimates-azura.csv (per-model projections).

If you want, I can add a small appendix with explicit node-count/expected-dollar-per-hour estimates for the pilot configuration (4 H100 + autoscale to 8 H100) — Jordan, would you like that included for procurement?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
